paragraphs.sourceText: Part ⅠWriting ( 30 minutes) Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay commenting on the saying" Never go out there to see what happens, go out there to make things happen." You can cit examples to illustrate the importance of being participants rather than mere onlookers in life. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第一部分写作（30分钟）说明：在这部分，你有30分钟的时间写一篇文章，评论“永远不要出去看看会发生什么，出去让事情发生。”你可以举一些例子来说明在生活中成为参与者而不是旁观者的重要性。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 36 to 45 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 36 至 45 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Children do not think the way adults do. For most of the first year of life, if something is out of sight, it's out of mind. If you cover a baby's36toy with a piece of cloth, the baby thinks the toyhas disappeared and stops looking for it. A 4-year-old may 37 that a sister has more fruit juice when it is only the shapes of the glasses that differ, not the38 of juice.

Yet children are smart in their own way. Like good little scientists, children are always testing their child-sized39 about how things work. When your child throws her spoon on the floor for the sixth time as you try to feed her, and you say, "That's enough! I will not pick up your spoon again!" the child will 40 test your claim. Are you serious? Are you angry? What will happen if she throws the spoon again? She is not doing this to drive you41; rather, she is learning that her desires and yours can differ, and that sometimes those42 are important and sometimes they are not.

How and why does children's thinking change? In the 1920s, Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget proposed that children's cognitive (认知的) abilities unfold 43, like the blooming of a flower, almost independent of what else is44in their lives. Although many of his specific conclusions havebeen45 or modified over the years, his ideas inspired thousands of studies by investigators all over the world.

Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with, ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.The Perfect Essay
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡上标记相应的字母来回答问题 2.完美作文

paragraphs.sourceText: A. Looking back on too many years of education, I can identify one truly impossible teacher. She cared about me, and my intellectual life, even when I didn't. Her expectations were high--impossibly so. She was an English teacher. She was also my mother.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：回顾多年的教育经历，我可以找出一位真正不可能的老师。她关心我和我的精神生活，即使我并不关心。她的期望很高——难以置信。她是一名英语老师。她也是我的母亲。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. When good students turn in an essay, they dream of their instructor returning it to them in exactly the same condition, save for a single word added in the margin of the final page : "Flawless." This dream came true for me one afternoon in the ninth grade. Of course, I had heard that genius could show itself at an early age, so I was only slightly taken aback that I had achieved perfection at the tender age of 14.Obviously, I did what any professional writer would do; I hurried off to spread the good news. I didn't get very far. The first person I told was my mother.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 当好学生交论文时，他们梦想着老师将论文以完全相同的状态返还给他们，除了在最后一页的空白处添加一个词：“完美”。这个梦想在我九年级的一个下午实现了。当然，我听说天才可以在很小的时候就显现出来，所以我对自己在14岁就达到完美只是感到有点惊讶。显然，我做了任何职业作家都会做的事情；我赶紧去传播这个好消息。我没走多远。我告诉的第一个人是我的母亲。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. My mother, who is just shy of five feet tall, is normally incredibly soft-spoken, but on the rare occasion when she got angry, she was terrifying. I am not sure if she was more upset by my hubris(得意忘形) or by the fact that my English teacher had let my ego get so out of hand. In any event, my mother and her red pen showed me how deeply flawed a flawless essay could be. At the time, I am sure she thought she was teaching me about mechanics, transitions (过渡), structure, style and voice. But what I learned, and what stuck with me through my time teaching writing at Harvard, was a deeper lesson about the nature of creative criticism.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 我的母亲身高不到五英尺，平时说话非常轻柔，但偶尔生气时却很可怕。我不确定她是因为我的傲慢而感到更加不安，还是因为我的英语老师让我的自我失控而感到更加不安。无论如何，我的母亲和她的红笔向我展示了一篇完美的论文可能存在多么严重的缺陷。当时，我确信她认为她正在教我有关机制、过渡、结构、风格和声音的知识。但我在哈佛教授写作期间学到的，以及一直困扰着我的，是关于创造性批评本质的更深刻的教训。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. First off, it hurts. Genuine criticism, the type that leaves a lasting mark on you as a writer, also leaves an existential imprint (印记) on you as a person. I have heard people say that a writer should never take criticism personally. I say that we should never listen to these people.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 首先，很痛。真正的批评会给你作为一个作家留下持久的印记，也会给你作为一个人留下存在主义的印记。我听人说作家永远不应该把批评当成是针对个人的。我说我们永远不应该听这些人的。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Criticism, at its best, is deeply personal, and gets to the heart of why we write the way we do. The intimate nature of genuine criticism implies something about who is able to give it, namely, someone who knows you well enough to show you how your mental life is getting in the way of good writing. Conveniently, they are also the people who care enough to see you through this painful realization. For me it took the form of my first, and I hope only, encounter with writer's block--I was not able to produce anything for three years.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 批评在最好的情况下是非常个人化的，并且触及我们为什么要这样写作的核心。真正的批评的亲密本质意味着谁能够给予批评，也就是说，一个足够了解你的人可以向你展示你的精神生活如何阻碍好的写作。方便的是，他们也是足够关心你并帮助你度过这个痛苦的人。对我来说，这就是我第一次，也是我唯一希望的，遭遇写作障碍——三年来我无法创作出任何作品。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. Franz Kafka once said: "Writing is utter solitude (独处), the descent into the cold abyss (深渊) of oneself." My mother's criticism had shown me that Kafka is right about the cold abyss, and when you make the introspective (内省的) descent that writing requires you are not always pleased by what you find. But, in the years that followed, her sustained tutoring suggested that Kafka might be wrong about the solitude. I was lucky enough to find a critic and teacher who was willing to make the journey of writing with me."It is a thing of no great difficulty," according to Plutarch, "to raise objections against another man's speech, it is a very easy matter; but to produce a better in its place is a work extremely troublesome." I am sure I wrote essays in the later years of high school without my mother's guidance, but I can't recall them. What I remember, however, is how she took up the "extremely troublesome" work of ongoing criticism.
paragraphs.translationZh: 卡夫卡曾经说过：“写作是完全的孤独，是坠入自我的冰冷的深渊。”我母亲的批评告诉我，卡夫卡关于寒冷深渊的看法是正确的，当你进行写作所要求的内省时，你并不总是对你所发现的东西感到满意。但是，在接下来的几年里，她持续的辅导表明卡夫卡对于孤独的看法可能是错误的。我很幸运地找到了一位愿意与我一起踏上写作旅程的评论家和老师。普鲁塔克说：“这并不是一件很困难的事情，对另一个人的演讲提出反对意见是一件很容易的事情；但要创作出更好的作品来代替它，那就是一件极其麻烦的事情了。”我确信我在高中最后几年在没有母亲指导的情况下写了论文，但我不记得了。然而，我记得的是她如何承担起持续批评的“极其麻烦”的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. There are two ways to interpret Plutarch when he suggests that a critic should be able to produce "a better in its place." In a straightforward sense, he could mean that a critic must be more talented than the artist she critiques (评论).My mother was well covered on this count. But perhaps Plutarch is suggesting something slightly different, something a bit closer to Marcus Cicero's claim that one should "criticize by creation, not by finding fault." Genuine criticism creates a precious opening for an author to become better on his own terms--a process that is often extremely painful, but also almost always meaningful.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 当普鲁塔克建议批评家应该能够“在其位置上创造出更好的作品”时，有两种解释方式。从直接的意义上来说，他的意思可能是批评家必须比她所批评的艺术家更有才华（评论）。我的母亲在这一点上得到了充分的体现。但也许普鲁塔克提出的建议略有不同，有点接近马库斯·西塞罗的主张，即人们应该“通过创造来批评，而不是通过挑剔”。真正的批评为作者创造了一个宝贵的机会，使他能够以自己的方式变得更好——这个过程通常是极其痛苦的，但也几乎总是有意义的。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. My mother said she would help me with my writing, but first I had to help myself. For each assignment, I was to write the best essay I could. Real criticism is not meant to find obvious mistakes, so if she found any--the type I could have found on my own--I had to start from scratch. From scratch. Once the essay was "flawless," she would take an evening to walk me through my errors. That was when true criticism, the type that changed me as a person, began.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 我妈妈说她会帮助我写作，但首先我必须帮助自己。对于每项作业，我都要写出最好的论文。真正的批评并不是为了发现明显的错误，所以如果她发现任何错误——我自己也可以找到的类型——我就必须从头开始。从头开始。一旦论文“完美无缺”，她就会花一个晚上的时间来纠正我的错误。就在那时，真正的批评开始了，这种批评改变了我的性格。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. She criticized me when I included little-known references and professional jargon (行话).She hadno patience for brilliant but irrelevant figures of speech."Writers can't bluff (虚张声势) their way through ignorance." That was news to me--I would need to freed another way to structure my daily existence.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一、当我加入鲜为人知的参考文献和行话时，她批评我。她对精彩但不相关的修辞格没有耐心。“作家不能通过无知虚张声势。”这对我来说是个新闻——我需要释放另一种方式来构建我的日常生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. She trimmed back my flowery language, drew lines through my exclamation marks and argued for the value of restraint in expression."John," she almost whispered. I leaned in to hear her: "I can't hear you when you shout at me." So I stopped shouting and bluffing, and slowly my writing improved.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 她削减了我华丽的语言，划清了我的感叹号，并论证了表达中克制的价值。“约翰，”她几乎低声说道。我凑过去听她说：“你对我喊我听不到。”于是我不再喊叫，不再虚张声势，我的写作也慢慢进步了。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Somewhere along the way I set aside my hopes of writing that flawless essay. But perhaps I missed something important in my mother's lessons about creativity and perfection. Perhaps the point of writing the flawless essay was not to give up, but to never willingly finish. Whit man repeatedly reworked "Song of Myself' between 1855 and 1891.Repeatedly.We do our absolute best with a piece of writing, and come as close as we can to the ideal. And, for the time being, we settle. In critique, however, we are forced to depart, to give up the perfection we thought we had achieved for the chance of being even a little bit better. This is the lesson I took from my mother: If perfection were possible, it would not be motivating.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 一路走来，我放弃了写那篇完美论文的希望。但也许我在母亲关于创造力和完美的课程中错过了一些重要的东西。也许写出完美论文的目的不是放弃，而是永不心甘情愿地完成。惠特曼在1855年至1891年间反复修改《我自己的歌》。反复。我们尽最大努力写一篇文章，尽可能接近理想。暂时，我们安定下来。然而，在批评中，我们被迫离开，放弃我们认为已经达到的完美，以获得更好一点的机会。这是我从母亲那里得到的教训：如果完美是可能的，那么它就不会是完美的。激励。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46.The author was advised against the improper use of figures of speech.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 有人建议提交人不要不当使用修辞手法。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47.The author's mother taught him a valuable lesson by pointing out lots of flaws in his seemingly perfect essay.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47.作者的母亲指出了他看似完美的论文中的许多缺陷，给他上了宝贵的一课。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48.A writer should polish his writing repeatedly so as to get closer to perfection.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48.作家应该反复打磨自己的作品，以接近完美。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49.Writers may experience periods of time in their life when they just can't produce anything.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49.作家一生中可能会经历一段无法创作任何作品的时期。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50.The author was not much surprised when his school teacher marked his essay as "flawless".
paragraphs.translationZh: 50.当作者的学校老师将他的论文标记为“完美无缺”时，他并不感到太惊讶。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51.Criticizing someone's speech is said to be easier than coming up with a better one.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51.据说批评某人的言论比提出更好的言论更容易。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52.The author looks upon his mother as his most demanding and caring instructor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52.提交人把他的母亲视为最严格、最关爱他的导师。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53.The criticism the author received from his mother changed him as a person.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53.提交人母亲的批评改变了他的性格。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54.The author gradually improved his writing by avoiding fancy language.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54.作者通过避免花哨的语言逐渐提高了他的写作水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55.Constructive criticism gives an author a good start to improve his writing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55.建设性批评为作者提高写作提供了良好的开端。

For each of them there are four choices marked A, B, C. and D .You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the center.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Could you reproduce Silicon Valley elsewhere, or is there something unique about it?
paragraphs.translationZh: 你能在其他地方重现硅谷吗？或者它有什么独特之处吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: It wouldn't be surprising if it were hard to reproduce in other countries, because you couldn't reproduce it in most of the US either. What does it take to make a Silicon Valley?
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果它在其他国家/地区难以复制也就不足为奇了，因为在美国大部分地区也无法复制它。打造硅谷需要什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: It's the right people. If you could get the right ten thousand people to move from Silicon Valley to Buffalo, Buffalo would become Silicon Valley.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这是对的人。如果你能让一万人从硅谷搬到布法罗，布法罗就会成为硅谷。

paragraphs.sourceText: You only need two kinds of people to create a technology hub (中心) : rich people and nerds (痴迷科研的人).
paragraphs.translationZh: 创建技术中心只需要两种人：富人和痴迷科研的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Observation bears this out. Within the US, towns have become star, up hubs if and only if they have both rich people and nerds. Few startups happen in Miami, for example, because although it's full of rich people, it has few nerds. It's not the kind of place nerds like.
paragraphs.translationZh: 观察证实了这一点。在美国，当且仅当城镇同时拥有富人和书呆子时，它们才能成为明星、上升中心。例如，很少有初创公司出现在迈阿密，因为尽管那里到处都是富人，但书呆子却很少。这不是书呆子喜欢的地方。

paragraphs.sourceText: Whereas Pittsburgh has the opposite problem: plenty of nerds, but no rich people.The top US Computer Science departments are said to be MIT, Stanford, Berkeley, and Carnegie-Mellon. MIT yielded Route 128.Stanford and Berkeley yielded Silicon Valley. But what did Carnegie-Mellon yield in Pittsburgh? And what happened in Ithaca, home of Cornell University, which is also high on the list?
paragraphs.translationZh: 而匹兹堡却有相反的问题：书呆子很多，但没有富人。据说美国顶尖的计算机科学系是麻省理工学院、斯坦福大学、伯克利分校和卡内基梅隆大学。麻省理工学院产生了128号公路。斯坦福和伯克利产生了硅谷。但卡内基梅隆大学在匹兹堡取得了什么成果呢？同样名列前茅的康奈尔大学所在地伊萨卡发生了什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: I grew up in Pittsburgh and went to college at Cornell, so I can answer for both. The weather is terrible, particularly in winter, and there's no interesting old city to make up for it, as there is in Boston. Rich people don't want to live in Pittsburgh or Ithaca. So while there're plenty of hackers (电脑迷) who could start startups, there's no one to invest in them
paragraphs.translationZh: 我在匹兹堡长大，在康奈尔大学上大学，所以我可以回答这两个问题。天气很糟糕，尤其是在冬天，而且没有像波士顿那样有趣的老城区来弥补这一点。有钱人不想住在匹兹堡或伊萨卡。因此，虽然有很多黑客（电脑迷）可以创办初创公司，但没有人投资他们

paragraphs.sourceText: Do you really need the rich people? Wouldn't it work to have the government invest in the nerds?
paragraphs.translationZh: 你真的需要有钱人吗？让政府投资于书呆子难道不行吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: No, it would not. Start up investors are a distinct type of rich people. They tend to have a lot of experience themselves in the technology business. This helps them pick the right startups, and means they can supply advice and connections as well as money. And the fact that they have a personal stake in the outcome makes them really pay attention.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不，不会的。初创投资者是一类独特的富人。他们往往在技术行业拥有丰富的经验。这有助于他们选择合适的初创公司，也意味着他们可以提供建议、人脉以及资金。事实上，他们与结果息息相关，这让他们真正关注。

paragraphs.sourceText: 56.What do we learn about Silicon Valley from the passage?
paragraphs.translationZh: 56.我们从这篇文章中了解到硅谷的什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 57.What makes Miami unfit to produce a Silicon Valley?
paragraphs.translationZh: 57.是什么让迈阿密不适合产生硅谷？

paragraphs.sourceText: 58.In what way is Carnegie-Mellon different from Stanford, Berkeley and MIT?
paragraphs.translationZh: 58.卡内基梅隆大学与斯坦福大学、伯克利大学和麻省理工学院有何不同？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: It's nice to have people of like mind around. Agreeable people boost your confidence and allow you to relax and feel comfortable. Unfortunately, that comfort can hinder the very learning that can expand your company and your career.
paragraphs.translationZh: 周围有志同道合的人真是太好了。和蔼可亲的人会增强你的信心，让你放松并感到舒适。不幸的是，这种舒适感可能会阻碍你的学习，而学习本身可以拓展你的公司和你的职业生涯。

paragraphs.sourceText: It's nice to have people agree, but you need conflicting perspectives to dig out the truth .If everyone around you has similar views, your work will suffer from confirmation bias (偏颇).
paragraphs.translationZh: 人们同意固然很好，但你需要相互冲突的观点来挖掘真相。如果你周围的每个人都有相似的观点，你的工作就会遭受确认偏差（偏颇）。

paragraphs.sourceText: Take a look at your own network. Do your contacts share your point of view on most subjects? If yes, it's time to shake things up .As a leader, it can be challenging to create an environment in which people will freely disagree and argue, but as the saying goes: From confrontation comes brilliance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 看看你自己的网络。您的联系人在大多数问题上都同意您的观点吗？如果是，那么是时候进行彻底改变了。作为领导者，创造一个人们可以自由表达不同意见和争论的环境可能具有挑战性，但俗话说：对抗产生智慧。

paragraphs.sourceText: It's not easy for most people to actively seek conflict. Many spend their lives trying to avoid arguments. There's no need to go out and find people you hate, but you need to do some self-assessment to determine where you have become stale in your thinking. You may need to start by encouraging your current network to help you identify your blind spots.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于大多数人来说，主动寻求冲突并不容易。许多人一生都在努力避免争论。没有必要出去寻找你讨厌的人，但你需要做一些自我评估，以确定你的思维在哪里变得陈旧。您可能需要首先鼓励您当前的网络来帮助您识别盲点。

paragraphs.sourceText: Passionate, energetic debate does not require anger and hard feelings to be effective. But it does require moral strength. Once you have worthy opponents, set some ground rules so everyone understands responsibilities and boundaries. The objective of this debating game is not to win but to get to the truth that will allow you to move faster, farther, and better.
paragraphs.translationZh: 充满激情、充满活力的辩论并不需要愤怒和怨恨才能有效。但这确实需要道德力量。一旦你有了有价值的对手，就制定一些基本规则，以便每个人都了解责任和界限。这个辩论游戏的目的不是为了获胜，而是为了了解真相，让你走得更快、更远、更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: Fierce debating can hurt feelings, particularly when strong personalities are involved. Make sure you check in with your opponents so that they are not carrying the emotion of the battles beyond the battlefield. Break the tension with smiles and humor to reinforce the idea that this is friendly discourse and that all are working toward a common goal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 激烈的辩论可能会伤害感情，尤其是当涉及到强势的人时。确保与对手沟通，以免他们将战斗情绪带到战场之外。用微笑和幽默打破紧张气氛，强化这样的观念：这是友好的对话，所有人都在朝着共同的目标努力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Reward all those involved in the debate sufficiently when the goals are reached. Let your sparring partners (拳击陪练) know how much you appreciate their contribution. The more they feel appreciated, the more they'll be willing to get into the ring next time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当目标达到时，充分奖励所有参与辩论的人。让你的陪练伙伴知道你是多么欣赏他们的贡献。他们越感到被欣赏，下次就越愿意参加比赛。
